description: Multi-subtree sweep across three identification edge cases. Subtree 0 (direct): two clearly-named products with detailed evaluations — straightforward. Subtree 1 (anaphoric): the dismissive-Corsair scenario from M1 — tests anaphoric reference resolution AND calibrated handling of an anti-recommendation. Subtree 2 (no product): a comment that explicitly says 'almost any 27" IPS panel works fine' — tests that the candidate does NOT hallucinate specific products from a generic recommendation, plus a one-word reply that should produce empty products. Runs 2 candidates with perCandidate: 3 so the per-comment table demonstrates the stacked-runs layout.

expectations.desiredOutcome: Default expectation: schema-valid JSON conforming to subtree-identification.schema, every PLAN comment receives an entry. Per-subtree overrides above describe the specific behaviors each subtree tests.

judge.instructions: Score each candidate on three dimensions, each 1-10: (1) faithfulness — exactly the products mentioned in each PLAN comment, no hallucinations, anaphoric references resolved when present? (2) calibration — does contentQuality match the depth of evaluation? high = detailed first-hand or reasoned; medium = short verdict; low = bare mention. (3) completeness — every PLAN comment has an entry, even if products is empty? Return JSON {candidates:[{candidateId, scores:{faithfulness,calibration,completeness}, rationale}], verdict}. Verdict format: 'best=<id>' | 'tie' | 'none-acceptable'.

expectations.desiredOutcome: Surface both Acer Predator X34 X5 (in ds-r1) with high contentQuality (first-hand owner with detailed evaluation) and ROG Swift PG34WCDM (in ds-r2) with medium-to-high quality (reasoned recommendation with rationale). Schema-valid JSON. No products hallucinated into either comment.

Surface LG 34GS95QE-B AND MSI MPG 341CQPX in an-r1 via anaphoric reference resolution from 'both are solid' (medium contentQuality — short verdict, no detail). ALSO surface Corsair Xeneon 34WQHD240-C with low or medium contentQuality reflecting that it's a buyer-relevant anti-recommendation. Surfacing only Corsair (dropping LG/MSI) is a faithfulness failure. Schema-valid JSON.

np-r1 contains a generic product class recommendation (any 27" 1440p IPS panel) but no specific brand+model pair. Candidates should produce an empty products array for np-r1 — hallucinating a specific product like 'Dell U2723QE' from this comment is a faithfulness failure. np-r2 ('Thanks, that's helpful!') has no product reference and must produce an empty products array. Schema-valid JSON.
